item.title: Carluccio Nursery School Como: staff writes to the Municipality
item.description: The staff of the Carluccio preschool on Via Volta writes to the Mayor to oppose the cuts: the school is not a cost, but a community investment.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - After September 28, the staff wrote a new letter. - Carluccio is the preschool on via Volta in Como. - The positive ruling: Carluccio remains open. - Signed by Bozzi, ten teachers and the school assistant.
## Key facts - Location → Carluccio preschool, via Volta, Como - Document → letter from Maria Grazia Bozzi - Signatories → ten teachers and the school assistant - Debate → reorganization involving closures and mergers - Precedent → closure decided by the Municipal Administration two years ago - Appeal → TAR, filed to defend the school - Outcome → positive ruling: Carluccio remains open - Symbol → olive tree given by Comitato Nova Como in September
After the City Council meeting of September 28, Carluccio preschool is once again at the center of the debate over the reorganization of schools in Como. The reorganization sought by the Rapinese administration provides for closures and mergers; the majority approved a resolution on the downsizing of schools. It is from this development that the new letter from the staff of the preschool on via Volta stems.
The letter is signed by Maria Grazia Bozzi, the school’s representative. The document also bears the signatures of ten teachers and the school assistant. The letter is addressed to the Mayor and the Councillor for Education and Educational Policies and argues that one cannot remain indifferent in the face of the resolution. The text makes clear that it does not intend to repeat the explanations already set out in previous letters concerning the effects of mergers and closures; instead, it chooses to return to the reality of Carluccio.
The text recalls what happened two years ago. The Municipal Administration had decided on the closure of the school. Families, committees, teachers and the entire school community did not remain indifferent to that decision. Thanks to the determination of the families, the committees and, in particular, Comitato Nova Como, together with the teachers and Istituto Comprensivo Como Borgovico, a campaign was launched to defend Carluccio. The process also led to an appeal to the TAR. Then came the positive ruling: the school remained open.
Teachers, parents and the entire Istituto Comprensivo Como Borgovico celebrated that decision, because Carluccio is not simply a place in which to welcome children. For the staff, it is a school founded on educational values, on a specific view of the child and on a pedagogical project built day after day. The letter thus calls into question an understanding of the school based solely on organizational or numerical criteria, as if it were merely the place where children are left while their parents work. The position expressed is unequivocal: Carluccio must be considered for what it represents educationally and within the community, not merely for its place in the reorganization of schools. ### An Educational Project Built Every Day
La Carluccio is described as a socio-educational hub in the heart of the city of Como. In the document, attention shifts from the organizational aspect to the meaning of preschool. It is the first educational environment in which children experience relationships with others, learn to share and communicate, recognize their own emotions and those of others, and gradually become independent. For the letter, these steps describe the school’s daily work.
The structure of the project moves from sections to spaces, from workshops to the schedule of the day and the stable presence of teachers. The document considers them integral parts of the educational project, not secondary components to be improvised. The environments must be designed to allow children to explore, experiment, play, create, and learn. The stable presence of teachers also has an educational and relational function: the reference figures know each child’s development, characteristics, vulnerabilities, and potential.
The word continuity occupies a central place in the letter. Continuity means not viewing each school year as an isolated experience, but building a path that accompanies the child as they grow. The educational thread must connect teachers, families, and the local community and, subsequently, preschool and primary school. Time and conditions are also needed to observe each child in their uniqueness: not everyone learns in the same way, not everyone has the same pace, and not everyone expresses their needs through words.
La Carluccio is also described as a place of inclusion. Differences can become a source of enrichment, and every child must be able to find their own space, feel part of the group, and develop their potential. This reading leads to criticism of an assessment based solely on the number of enrolled children, the spaces occupied, or a financial statement. A school is made up of relationships, skills, experiences, professionalism, and community. La Carluccio, the staff writes, represents all of this.
Another element mentioned in the letter is the olive tree donated to the school by Comitato Nova Como last school year, in September. The tree was chosen as a symbol of rebirth, strength, and resilience. For teachers and school staff, it aptly represents the school: once again, they have started anew with determination and passion, continuing to believe in the value of their work and in the strength of the educational project. ### The request to listen to the community
The letter indicates the criterion to follow before making decisions about Carluccio's future. The staff asks that those who experience the school every day be listened to: the children, families, teachers and all the school staff. The document specifies that the value of the school concerns not only the families who attend it today, but the entire community. For this reason, the assessment of its future should not stop at the premises, the numbers or the economic dimension mentioned in the text.
The point called for by the authors therefore concerns recognizing the network built over time. According to the letter, closing or scaling back a preschool would mean breaking up a network of relationships and weakening an educational hub. That network includes the relationship between children, families, teachers and the local area, along with the path connecting preschool to primary school. Carluccio is thus presented as an institution that belongs to the community, not merely to the families who attend it today.
The document then returns to the image of roots. Carluccio school has already shown that it has deep roots, and the olive tree donated by Comitato Nova Como has become their symbol. Those roots, the staff writes, ask to be respected, nurtured and allowed to grow. Behind a school there are not only walls and numbers: there are children, people, relationships, an educational project and a community. The letter links to this heritage the idea that a community capable of investing in its children also invests in its future.
The signatures make the position expressed in the document a collective one. In addition to the representative Maria Grazia Bozzi, the teachers Angelica Sansone, Giorgia Marchio, Paola Della Bosca, Sabrina Ghielmetti, Domenica Previtali, Virginia Fiandaca, Manuela Ghislanzoni, Lucia D'Angelo, Francesca Pellegrino and Silvana Somaini sign. The school support staff member identified is Nunzia Battista.
> «The school is not a cost to be reduced: it is an investment to be protected.»
This is the phrase with which the staff summarizes the request for protection addressed to those who will have to deal with the future of the Carluccio preschool.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/como-lettera-da-tutto-il-personale-dellasilo-carluccio-la-scuola-non-e-un-costo-da-ridurre-qui-ce-una-comunita/)*

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Varese host Pergine on Saturday at 18.30 - Mastini and Linci are on 3 points - Vanetti and Terzago remain out - Franchini may be called up
## Key facts - Game → Varese-Pergine - Venue → Acinque Ice Arena - Standings → Varese, Pergine and Feltre are on 3 points - Absences → Vanetti and Terzago - Shots on goal → Varese 35, Caldaro 33 - Power play → figure reversed compared with last year
At 18.30 on Saturday, Varese's Mastini host Pergine at the Acinque Ice Arena. It is a direct clash between two mid-table teams: Varese, Pergine and Feltre are level on 3 points, six points behind the Caldaro-Aosta duo. The game is part of the fourth matchday of the IHL and comes after the Mastini's away game at Caldaro.
The game in South Tyrol left one certainty and one obligation. The certainty concerns the character of the team coached by Dave Rich. Trailing 3-0 after less than nine minutes, the black-and-yellow side got back into the game in the second period. Then Selva's goal, scored 11 seconds before the second buzzer, shifted the momentum toward the Lucci, who managed to confirm their superiority in the third period.
The obligation is to turn that reaction into points against a Pergine side described as a strong team. The Linci will also bring their supporters to the Acinque Ice Arena, while Varese will have to reproduce the quick attacks and offensive play shown in the last outing.
### A team with more options
Against Caldaro, the Mastini finished with 35 shots on goal, compared with 33 attempts by their opponents. The numbers reflect an attack with several options: Bastille, De Toni, Borghi, Piroso and the new arrival Glasman are listed among the most dangerous players up front.
The defense also offered positive signs, although it needs reinforcements to preserve energy and focus. Filippo Matonti was once again among the best. Among the goaltenders, Leonardo Mordenti's return home is also noted. Another positive element is the power play, described as completely transformed compared with last year.
### The roster and the home-ice factor
Dave Rich will decide whether to dress Franchini based on the forward's physical condition. Captain Vanetti will remain out for around twenty days because of a muscle problem, while Terzago is still unavailable. The absence of both forces the defense to operate with a five-man rotation.
The performances against Fassa and Caldaro are presented as an incentive to fill the arena. According to the game preview, the black-and-yellow faithful will have to be the extra man on the ice. The comparison between Varese and Pergine’s campaigns explains why the game has the profile of a direct clash, without turning the standings into a prediction. After three matchdays, both teams have 3 points, along with Feltre, while Caldaro and Aosta lead with 9.
| Team | Campaign in the opening matchdays | |---|---| | Varese | Home defeat to Appiano 2-4; win at Fassa 5-3; away game at Caldaro | | Pergine | Home defeat to Fassa 3-6; comeback against Val Pusteria Junior 4-3; home defeat to Appiano 1-5 |
The most useful reference point is Fassa. Varese won on its ice, while Pergine lost at home against the same team. It is the comparison that warrants a fair degree of optimism, but the same source reminds us that every game is a story unto itself. The outcome of the direct clash will therefore depend on the ability to reproduce the positive indications on the ice, not merely on the sequence of previous games.
### The Linci profile
Pergine should not be underestimated either because of last season’s campaign. The Linci of Valsugana finished fifth and, in the playoff quarterfinals, immediately overturned home-ice advantage against Appiano. This is a precedent that supports a cautious reading of the game.
James Thomas Dowd is the name identified as the main offensive reference point. He has already scored against Fassa and Appiano and has been well supported by Foccoli, Bitetto and Dellmar Speranza. Andreotti, meanwhile, is described as a player capable of striking in crucial moments. Defensively, some uncertainty remains in the Linci’s setup: this is the weak point the Mastini will have to try to exploit.
### The key to the clash
The game therefore pits Varese’s offensive variety against an opponent that has shown quality, but also possible vulnerability at the back. The Pergine crowd will be passionate, while the yellow-and-black crowd is called upon to support the team at the Acinque Ice Arena. 1. Check Varese's lineup. The decision regarding Franchini will depend on the forward's physical condition. Vanetti and Terzago remain out, forcing the defense to rotate with five men.
2. Watch the start. In Caldaro, the Mastini were down 3-0 after less than nine minutes, but they reacted in the second period. Managing the start will therefore be one of the first elements to observe.
3. Measure offensive production. Against Caldaro, Varese shot 35 times, while their opponents finished 33 times. Fast transitions and the ability to involve Bastille, De Toni, Borghi, Piroso, and Glasman represent the benchmarks indicated on the eve of the match.

item.title: Hockey, Ambrì conquer the BCF Arena: Fribourg beaten 2-1
item.description: After two defeats, Ambrì rediscover their solidity and win 2-1 in Fribourg. Goals by Müller and Schnarr prove decisive in an evening of great defensive sacrifice.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ambrì wins 2-1 on Friborgo's ice - Müller and Schnarr score the decisive goals - Pestoni returns in place of the suspended Borradori - At 12', Miles Müller puts the blue-and-whites ahead
## Key facts - Result → 2-1 for Ambrì - Arena → BCF Arena - Return → Inti Pestoni - Absence → Tim Heed - Defense → six regular defensemen - Penalty kill → 66,6% before the game - Goaltending choice → Galley preferred to Waeber
After two consecutive home defeats, Ambrì were looking for crucial points in the den of the Swiss champions. At BCF Arena, the response came with a 2-1 victory, built on solidity, sacrifice and efficiency—in other words, the elements Tapola wanted to rediscover. The blue-and-whites thus conquered Friborgo's rink with full merit.
### A response after the home defeats
The lineup also presented some difficulties. Inti Pestoni returned to the lineup in place of the suspended Borradori, alongside Joly and Kodytek. In addition, Tapola had to deal with Tim Heed's absence, taking the ice with just six regular defensemen.
Despite the depleted defense, Ambrì started strongly, immediately putting the Swiss champions under pressure. Pestoni also looked dangerous, but was unable to beat Galley, preferred to Waeber. A penalty to Grassi in the offensive zone temporarily halted the Leventine side's momentum.
Friborgo's subsequent power play was neutralized by the blue-and-white penalty kill, though not without a few scares. Before the game, that special-teams situation was the worst in the League, with just 66,6% success.
At 12', Ambrì took the lead. Streule's mistake paved the way for Miles Müller, who made no mistake. Shortly afterward, Schmid hit a glaring post, but the visitors continued to create the best chances. The first period ended with Ambrì ahead and having rediscovered themselves after the last two outings. Müller and Schnarr's goals then decided an evening that ended with the blue-and-whites' 2-1 victory. ## The tactical key to victory
### Compactness, transitions and management of key moments
Ambrì's 2-1 win can be understood through a game plan that remained recognizable over the three periods. The team started strongly, maintained a compact and aggressive approach in the middle period and preserved the same identity at the start of the third period. The willingness to break forward accompanied the defensive phase without turning it into a passive approach.
The first element concerns precisely the ability to stick to Tapola's plan when Friborgo increased the pressure. The Swiss champions grew stronger in the middle period, but Wüthrich was ready on shots from Sörensen and Bertschy. At the same time, the blue-and-whites did not give up on the counterattack: Järventie found himself all alone in front of Galley with the puck for the second goal on his stick, but was unable to convert.
The second element is the management of the penalty kill. Grassi's penalty in the offensive zone had given Friborgo the opportunity to exploit the numerical advantage. The blue-and-white unit nevertheless neutralized the power play, despite a few moments of concern. The 66,6% figure makes this passage even more significant in the story of the game, because the special-teams situation entered the match as the worst in the League.
The third element is the resistance in the third period. Friborgo increased the pace, driven above all by Sörensen's line, but Ambrì responded with short shifts, great intensity and maximum focus. When the defense and Wüthrich were not enough, the post intervened once again: Nemeth's shot, shortly before the halfway point of the period, made the home cage tremble. The performance therefore stemmed from the balance between chances created, pressure absorbed and the ability to remain faithful to the game plan.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to read Ambrì's performance
### Four checks in the match report
To follow the game without focusing solely on the result, it is useful to start with the choices that defined the evening. The match report offers a precise sequence, useful for linking lineups, incidents and the team's response.
- Lineup and absences. The first step is to consider Inti Pestoni's return, brought in for the suspended Borradori, alongside Joly and Kodytek. In the same context, one must place Tim Heed's absence and the presence of just six regular defensemen.
- Start and special teams. The second step is to observe Ambrì's aggressive start, Pestoni's threat and Grassi's penalty in the offensive zone. The penalty kill should be read alongside the 66,6% recorded before the game and the ability to neutralize Fribourg's power play.
- Offensive incidents. The third step concerns efficiency. Streule's error paved the way for Miles Müller at 12', while Schmid's shot off the post and Järventie's chance in front of Galley show the other opportunities created by the blue-and-whites.
- Final pressure. The final check concerns the response to the pace imposed by Fribourg. Sörensen's line pushed forward, but Ambrì maintained short shifts, intensity and focus. Wüthrich dealt with the opponents' shots, and the post also denied Nemeth.
This framework makes it possible to read the performance through its essential stages, without separating Pestoni's return from the collective performance and without overlooking the importance of the chances that went unconverted. Follow Ambrì's next sports reports on Frontaliere Ticino.

item.title: Luino, bottle caps with nails in the parking lot behind Tigros
item.description: Paolo Nicastri reports the presence of caps with nails pointing upwards in the area used by cars, motorcycles and driving schools for driving exams and tests.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Corks with nails found in the parking lot behind Tigros - The points were facing upward - The area is used by cars, motorcycles and driving schools - The report was made by Paolo Nicastri
## Key facts - Location → parking lot behind Tigros in Luino - Objects → cork stoppers with nails pointing upward - Report → Paolo Nicastri - Role → former mayoral candidate in Luino - Elections → May 2026 - Use of the area → cars, motorcyclists and driving schools - Driving-school activities → practice sessions and exams for a motorcycle license
Some cork stoppers with nails inserted and the points facing upward were reportedly found in the parking lot behind Tigros in Luino. Paolo Nicastri, a young man from Luino and former candidate for mayor of Luino in the May 2026 municipal elections, made the discovery public through social media.
The site is frequented by cars and motorcyclists and is also used by driving schools for practice sessions and exams for a motorcycle license. The presence of the corks therefore concerns an area where different users move around and where practical training activities also take place.
In the published video, Nicastri shows some corks into which nails appear to have been inserted. The points are oriented upward. The young man from Luino highlights the risk that a motorcyclist might ride over them, puncture a tire and fall. His question in the video draws attention to the possible immediate consequences of those objects being present on the ground.
The focus of the report is the physical danger posed by the nails and the particular use of the parking lot. Nicastri links the discovery to the safety of those who use the area, with specific attention to students taking part in practice sessions and exams for a motorcycle license.
The report published on social media therefore starts from this concrete element: the presence of sharp objects, with the points facing upward, in a Luino parking lot frequented by cars, motorcycles and driving schools. ## A parking lot also used for motorcycle tests
The role of driving schools is the point Nicastri emphasizes most in the video. He does not merely recall that the parking lot is frequented by motorcyclists: he stresses that practice sessions and motorcycle license tests take place in the same space. The presence of the nails is therefore described in relation to those who might cross the area during a training or examination activity.
> It is precisely in this parking lot that driving schools conduct practice sessions and motorcycle license exams
In his reasoning, the risk concerns not only the possible fall of a young person on a motorcycle. Nicastri also raises the possibility that a driving-school vehicle could puncture one or more tires by driving over the nails. In that case, he observes, the danger to people would be accompanied by financial damage. The report is thus linked both to physical safety and to the material consequences for those who use the parking lot.
The video also refers to some complaints that, according to Nicastri, have concerned the area recently. The reference is not turned into an accusation against anyone. Instead, the young man from Luino asks that any disputes over the use of the area be handled without adopting behavior capable of endangering other people.
The message also addresses the issue of motorcycle enthusiasts. Nicastri wonders whether it is possible to identify a dedicated and safe space for them, alongside the discussion of the risks present in a parking lot used for traffic and driving-school activities.
The reaction described by the source therefore remains a position conveyed through social media: safety for those taking the tests, attention to possible tire damage, and a request not to let complaints about the area degenerate into dangerous acts. ## The clarification about who left the caps
Paolo Nicastri accompanies the report with a clear clarification regarding responsibility for the act. He says he does not know who left the objects in the parking lot and makes it clear that he does not want to accuse anyone without concrete evidence. In the video, he states that he has no proof. His report, therefore, does not identify anyone responsible and keeps the discovery of the caps separate from any possible attribution of the act.
This passage also defines the scope of the matter described by the source. The issue reported at present is the presence of cork stoppers with nails pointing upward and the danger they may pose to cars, motorcycles and driving schools. Nicastri does not identify who allegedly left them, focusing his report on the objects found and their position in the parking lot.
The video’s conclusion returns specifically to safety. For the former mayoral candidate, the combination of nails pointing upward and a parking lot frequented by vehicles and motorcyclists constitutes an enormous danger. In his words, the same assessment applies to an area where driving schools take students for practice sessions and motorcycle license exams.
The continuation documented by the source contains neither an indication of who did it nor any further reconstruction of the act. item.title: Serious accident on the A2 in Coldrerio
item.description: Southbound rear-end collision: a 68-year-old woman was slightly injured, while the 73-year-old passenger is in serious condition.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Accident on Friday shortly before 15.30 on the A2 in Coldrerio - A car rear-ended a stationary articulated lorry in the emergency bay - The 73-year-old passenger was taken to hospital by helicopter - The A2 was closed and then reduced to one lane
## Key facts - Location → A2, southbound, Coldrerio area - Time → Friday, shortly before 15.30 - Driver → 68-year-old Swiss woman, resident in the Canton of Zurich - Passenger → 73-year-old Swiss man, resident in the Canton of Zurich - Conditions → woman slightly injured; man in serious condition - Traffic → temporary closure, then traffic on one lane - Responders → SAM, REGA, firefighters and cantonal police
### The initial account of the accident
On Friday afternoon, shortly before 15.30, a serious accident occurred on the A2 motorway in the southbound direction, in the Coldrerio area. The cantonal police reported that a 68-year-old Swiss woman, resident in the Canton of Zurich, rear-ended an articulated lorry stopped beside the carriageway, in the emergency bay. The causes of the collision will have to be established by the investigation.
Also travelling in the car was a 73-year-old Swiss passenger, likewise resident in the Canton of Zurich. After initial treatment, both were taken to hospital. The woman was taken by ambulance with minor injuries. The man, however, was transported by helicopter in serious condition; his life is in danger.
To allow rescue operations and the landing of the REGA helicopter, the carriageway was temporarily closed. Subsequently, traffic was funnelled into a single lane. The measure had a very significant impact on traffic.
The involvement of two people required two separate transports, by ambulance for the driver and by helicopter for the passenger. The difference in the modes of transport corresponds to the conditions reported by the police: minor injuries for the woman, serious condition for the man.
The rescue operation involved SAM rescuers, a REGA helicopter, firefighters from the Mendrisiotto rescue centre and the cantonal police. The investigation will have to establish the causes of the rear-end collision. ## Traffic difficulties in the Mendrisiotto
The temporary closure of the motorway and the subsequent reduction to a single lane had very significant consequences for traffic. At 5 p.m., the police advised against setting off southbound. The warning was issued while rescue operations had already affected mobility in the area.
### The roads affected
According to Viasuisse, in the late afternoon traffic was completely congested on all roads between Mendrisio and Genestrerio. The situation did not affect only the motorway route: the report also included the cantonal road between Mendrisio and Chiasso, the San Martino fork toward Melide and, in Lugano, the main roads in the city center.
| Area | Reported situation | |---|---| | Roads between Mendrisio and Genestrerio | Traffic completely congested | | Cantonal road between Mendrisio and Chiasso | Traffic completely congested | | San Martino fork toward Melide | Traffic completely congested | | Main roads in central Lugano | Traffic completely congested |
Viasuisse’s reports therefore covered a series of different connections: the stretch between the two centers of the Mendrisiotto, the cantonal road toward Chiasso, the road at the San Martino fork in the direction of Melide and the central streets of Lugano. All these points were completely congested in the late afternoon.
The picture provided by Viasuisse shows that the repercussions were not concentrated solely at the site of the accident. The closure and the switch to one lane affected traffic in several areas, while the police advice at 5 p.m. urged people to avoid traveling south.
The situation then improved after 8 p.m. This is the latest time-based update reported by the source on traffic conditions, following the congestion reported in the late afternoon. ## The investigation remains open
### The aftermath of the operation
The aftermath of the accident remains linked to the investigation into how it happened. The cantonal police indicated that it will have to establish the reasons why the motorist rear-ended the articulated lorry stopped in the emergency lay-by. The essential details of the reconstruction thus remain established: the collision occurred on the A2, heading south, in the territory of Coldrerio, with a heavy vehicle stopped at the side of the carriageway. The investigation will have to clarify the sequence of events that led to the collision.
The operational follow-up is already defined by the sequence of the rescue efforts. After receiving initial treatment, the two people were taken to hospital: the woman by ambulance and the man by helicopter. To allow the rescue operation and the landing of the REGA helicopter, the carriageway was temporarily closed; later, traffic was channelled into a single lane. SAM rescuers, the REGA helicopter, firefighters from the Mendrisiotto rescue centre and the cantonal police attended the scene.
The medical situation reported for the passenger also remains: the 73-year-old man was transported by helicopter in serious condition and his life is in danger. The 68-year-old woman, on the other hand, was taken to hospital by ambulance with minor injuries. The police statement therefore distinguishes between two different outcomes and leaves the follow-up of the investigation into how the accident happened open.

item.title: Gallarate: 22-year-old accused of robbery and violence
item.description: A 22-year-old man was reported while at liberty for aggravated robbery and sexual assault following an attack near the station in Gallarate; the victim, a 36-year-old woman, was discharged with a prognosis of seven days.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A 22-year-old reported for aggravated robbery and sexual assault - Assault in the area of Gallarate station - The woman discharged with a prognosis of seven days - The young man identified by the woman at the barracks
## Key facts - Charge → aggravated robbery and sexual assault - Young man's age → 22 years - Location → Gallarate railway station - Date → early hours of Thursday 21 September - Intervention → via Curioni, around one in the morning - Hospital → Sant'Antonio Abate di Gallarate - Prognosis → seven days - Outcome → reported while at liberty
### The intervention in Gallarate In the early hours of Thursday 21 September, in the area of Gallarate railway station, the Carabinieri intervened after an emergency call came in to 112. The incident led to a 22-year-old being reported while at liberty, accused of aggravated robbery and sexual assault.
The first intervention was carried out by officers from the Operational and Radiomobile Unit at around one in the morning, in via Curioni. On site, they found a woman alone, described as being in an evident state of shock, and provided her with first aid. The call therefore drew the officers' attention to the area near the railway station, where the woman had asked for help.
The woman told the officers that she had been approached shortly beforehand by a young man and that her mobile phone had been forcibly taken. The account concerns an evening spent with some friends and a subsequent assault in the station area. According to the officers' reconstruction, the phone theft was accompanied by sexual violence and physical consequences.
After the request for help, the officers began investigations at the scene. The text thus links the call to 112, the assistance provided in via Curioni and the investigation launched by the Gallarate Station. The events were reconstructed based on the woman's account and the officers' immediate checks.
The charges communicated concern two allegations: aggravated robbery and sexual assault. The young man, identified in the source as 22 years old, was reported while at liberty. The report places the Carabinieri intervention in the station area and links the reconstruction to the call to 112, the assistance provided in via Curioni and the checks carried out by the Gallarate Station.
The account therefore includes Piazza Giovanni XXIII, where the woman was spending the evening, the area near the railway station and via Curioni, where the officers provided first aid. These are the places indicated in the source to describe the beginning of the incident and the intervention by the Carabinieri. ## The reconstruction of the night
The sequence recounted to the officers begins at Piazza Giovanni XXIII, where the woman was spending the evening with some friends. After her cellphone was taken, she followed the young man in an attempt to get the smartphone back. The young man was riding an electric scooter, and the route led to the vicinity of the railway station, on Via Curioni.
According to the officers' reconstruction, the young man took advantage of the absence of passersby to attack the woman. He restrained her, tore her T-shirt, and forced her to submit to groping and sexual acts. The same reconstruction reports that the assault caused her physical injuries and abrasions.
During the frantic moments of the assault, the woman noticed a medium-sized kitchen knife. The man had it hidden in the waistband of his trousers. The detail of the knife appears in the officers' reconstruction together with the description of the absence of passersby.
The passing of a pedestrian interrupted the violence. The young man fled, and the woman was able to raise the alarm and request help. The officers found her in a state of shock when they arrived on Via Curioni.
### The hospital visit After receiving initial assistance, the woman was transported under a green code to the emergency department of the Sant'Antonio Abate Hospital in Gallarate. The transfer was for the necessary clinical examinations and dressings. Medical staff found various superficial wounds and then discharged her with a seven-day prognosis for recovery.
The visit to the emergency department represents the subsequent medical stage after the initial assistance provided on Via Curioni. The source indicates the green code, the clinical examinations, the dressings, the superficial wounds, and the discharge with a seven-day prognosis. The discharge came after the examinations and dressings, with the seven-day period indicated for recovery. ## Developments in the investigation
The inquiries by the Gallarate Carabinieri Station began immediately, after the woman filed her complaint on 21 September. The source indicates that the officers worked from the earliest stages of the case to determine the identity of the alleged perpetrator. According to the text, the result came within a few hours.
The young man was traced to his home and taken to the station. The source describes him as a 22-year-old of Peruvian origin. At the station, the victim recognized him without a shadow of a doubt. This step is reported before the young man was referred to the Judicial Authority.
### From the complaint to the referral The term used in the report for the outcome of the inquiries is referral to the Judicial Authority. The young man was therefore reported without being detained on charges of aggravated robbery and sexual assault. The source also reports that the investigation is continuing in close coordination with the authority to establish every detail of the case.
The investigative chronology indicated is brief but precise: complaint on 21 September, immediate inquiries, identification within a few hours, being traced at his home, being taken to the station, and recognition by the woman. After these steps, the 22-year-old was referred to the Judicial Authority.
The source also points out a discrepancy in the indication of the woman's age: the opening says 35, while the section on the reconstruction and the headline identify her as 36. The information is reported this way in the source; the investigative developments, however, remain those attributed to the Carabinieri of the Gallarate Station: identification of the young man, recognition at the station, and continuation of the investigation to clarify the case.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Two international podium finishes for Martina Bonalumi - Bronze at the FISU World University Championships in Ontario - Silver at the Under-23 European Championships in Kruszwica - Mayor Moro celebrates the team and its educational value
## Key facts - Protagonist → Martina Bonalumi - Role → coxswain of the Italian women's eight - First result → bronze in Ontario, Canada - Second result → silver in Kruszwica, Poland - Final → second place behind Romania - Community → Dumenza - Mayor → Corrado Nazario Moro - Federation → Italian Rowing Federation
Two international podium finishes within just a few weeks have placed Martina Bonalumi's name at the center of Dumenza's pride. item.title: Como, drug dealer arrested for home deliveries
item.description: The State Police of Como arrested a 48-year-old man: 51.45 grams of cocaine in 86 doses, 120 euros, and another 141.18 grams of cocaine seized.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A 48-year-old man arrested in Como for possession with intent to distribute - Cocaine home deliveries in the city and outskirts confirmed - 86 doses of cocaine and 51.45 grams seized - Ordered to be held at Bassone di Como
## Key facts - Who → 48-year-old Italian citizen of Dominican origin - Operation → Mobile Squad of the Como State Police - Method → home deliveries using his own car - Personal and vehicle seizure → 51.45 grams in 86 doses - Money → 120 euros believed to be proceeds from drug dealing - Phones → 2, used to contact customers - Home search → approximately 4000 euros and 141.18 grams - Outcome → arrest in the act and transfer to Bassone di Como
### The operation in Como
The State Police of Como arrested a 48-year-old Italian citizen of Dominican origin, legally residing in Italy. The man was found in possession of numerous doses of cocaine and cash.
The intervention took place during an operation conducted by investigators from the Mobile Squad to combat itinerant drug dealing. The counter-drug activity covered the city and outskirts.
Investigators established several sales of narcotics attributed to the 48-year-old. According to the reconstruction, the man carried out the activity using his own car, making home deliveries for the benefit of some users.
The sales were established during the Mobile Squad's work as part of the operation against drug dealing. The method described by the Police thus includes the use of the car and home delivery, while the investigation led to the identification of the person involved and some users.
After verifying the sales, the officers proceeded to identify and search the 48-year-old and his vehicle. The operation records also included a home search. The checks therefore concerned the man, his car, and his home, following a sequence of checks that preceded the arrest in the act described in the records. ## Seizures uncovered during the checks
### The personal and vehicle search
The personal and vehicle search led to the seizure of 51.45 grams of cocaine, divided into 86 doses. The police also seized 120 euros in cash, considered proceeds from drug dealing, and two phones used by the 48-year-old to contact customers. These items were seized during the check of the drug dealer, together with the substance already divided into doses.
| Check | Outcome | |---|---| | Personal and vehicle | 51.45 grams of cocaine in 86 doses; 120 euros; 2 phones | | Residence | Approximately 4000 euros in banknotes of different denominations; an additional 141.18 grams of cocaine |
### The search of the residence
The search of the residence led to the seizure of approximately 4000 euros in banknotes of different denominations and an additional 141.18 grams of cocaine. The seizure carried out at the residence is listed separately from the 51.45 grams divided into 86 doses found during the personal and vehicle search.
The two phones were used by the 48-year-old to contact customers, while the 120 euros were considered proceeds from drug dealing. The search of the residence added both more cocaine and a sum in banknotes of different denominations. The description of the seizures therefore distinguishes the material recovered during the personal and vehicle search from that found at the residence, reporting separately the two quantities of cocaine indicated in the records. ## The judicial follow-up
### The Judicial Authority's decision
At the conclusion of the proceedings, the 48-year-old was arrested in flagrante delicto for possession of narcotic substances with intent to distribute. Following his arrest, he was placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority. The authority ordered that the man be committed to Bassone Prison in Como.
The judicial stage comes after the identification and the personal, vehicle and home searches described in the operation. The charge brought against the 48-year-old remains possession of narcotic substances with intent to distribute, while the facility indicated for his commitment is Bassone Prison in Como.
For the recipients of the handovers, the subsequent course was different. Some were subsequently identified and administratively sanctioned. The sanction was imposed after investigators from the Mobile Squad established the handovers, in the operation against mobile drug dealing.
The concluding sequence described by the Police therefore comprises the arrest in flagrante delicto, being placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority, and the order committing him to Bassone in Como. These are the measures indicated for the 48-year-old after the searches and the seizure of the cocaine, cash and phones.
The outcome for the other recipients, on the other hand, is identification followed by an administrative sanction. The case thus keeps separate the measure adopted against the 48-year-old and the one concerning the recipients of the handovers. For the man, the place indicated by the Judicial Authority is Bassone Prison in Como.

The period between 15 September and 2 October 2026 saw the Como Local Police engaged in targeted monitoring and prevention operations in the Crocifisso area and at the Giardini di viale Varese. The officers paid particular attention to the areas identified as enhanced-protection zones, as part of the activity focused on strengthening urban security.
The selection of the locations is linked, in the Local Police's communication, to the presence of urban decay and conduct contrary to regulatory provisions. The main outcome of the activity was the issuance of 16 orders to leave, issued following violations of the provisions set out in the Urban Police Regulations and committed in the areas covered by the specific protection measures.
During the checks, four foreign nationals were also referred to the judicial authorities. This figure is indicated as a further result of the operations carried out in the areas subject to enhanced protection and adds to the orders to leave adopted for violations of the urban regulations.
The account of the operation therefore provides the tally of a series of targeted operations: territorial monitoring covered two locations identified for enhanced protection, led to removal measures and resulted in referrals to the judicial authorities. The activity was carried out by the Como Local Police as part of urban prevention and security efforts. ## How the outcomes are divided
The balance of the checks includes two types of outcomes. On one hand, there are removal orders, linked to violations of the Urban Police Regulations in the areas affected by protection measures. On the other hand, there are referrals to the judicial authority, for which the source distinguishes two different reasons.
The distinction reported by the Local Police is as follows:
| Outcome | Detail | |---|---| | Removal orders | 16 measures following violations of the Urban Police Regulations | | Immigration legislation | 2 subjects reported for violations related to this matter | | DACUR | 2 subjects reported for non-compliance with measures issued by the Questore of Como |

The framework thus includes interventions in reinforced protection zones and the various outcomes produced during the same activity. ## The checks will continue
The Como Local Police has indicated that checks in the areas under enhanced protection will also continue in the coming weeks. The continuation concerns the areas already identified for the specific protection measures. Reference therefore remains to the Crocifisso area and the Giardini di viale Varese, the same places where officers carried out operations between 15 settembre and 2 ottobre 2026. The communication links the continuity of the action to urban security planning.
For the coming weeks, the plan described keeps control of the areas under enhanced protection at its center. The stated objective remains the strengthening of urban security in areas affected by degradation phenomena and conduct contrary to regulatory provisions. The continuation confirms the ongoing nature of the services announced by the Local Police.
The checks carried out and the outcomes already recorded will be followed by further targeted operations. The Como Local Police will continue to operate within its urban security planning, with control and prevention activities in the areas designated as under enhanced protection. item.title: Historical Museum at Palazzo Civico: cross-party motion in Lugano
item.description: Ten city councillors ask to evaluate a historical museum on the second floor of Palazzo Civico, which will be liberated in 2028 with the move to Cornaredo.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A motion proposes a historical museum at Palazzo Civico - Ten municipal councillors support the request - The second floor could become available in 2028 - The East Tower of the Pse is planned for the relocation
## Key facts - Proposal → historical museum in the spaces of Palazzo Civico - First signatory → Danilo Baratti, Verdi e Indipendenti - Signatories → ten municipal councillors - Location → Palazzo Civico di Lugano - Relocation → part of the administration to Cornaredo, East Tower of the Pse - Second floor → office move scheduled for 2028 - Exhibition → Lugano Belle Époque, extended until 8 January next year - Building → neoclassical
Ten municipal councillors in Lugano are asking for the creation of a historical museum in the spaces of Palazzo Civico. The motion is cross-party and its first signatory is Danilo Baratti, of Verdi e Indipendenti. The building houses the municipal chancellery, the wedding hall, the municipal councillors’ offices and the Municipal Council chamber.
The starting point is the transfer, planned in a few years’ time, of part of the city administration to Cornaredo, in the East Tower of the Polo sportivo e degli eventi, the Pse. The motion focuses in particular on the second floor, which would be vacated by the relocation of the Municipal Administration offices planned for 2028. The parliamentary motion calls for the future of those spaces not to be left undecided.
According to the proponents, the intended use of the spaces should be discussed before any decisions are made about their use. The text points to the risk that, in the absence of preliminary consideration of a public use, the City could end up granting them to the first commercial bidder. The motion also links this risk to the need to cover the substantial rent of the East Tower.
### A decision about the building’s future
The document defines Palazzo Civico as a public building with strong symbolic value and calls for a debate to be opened on its future. The request concerns the use of some of the spaces that could become available, not the abandonment of the entire building. Lugano Deputy Mayor Roberto Badaracco has in fact stated that the building will not be decommissioned.
According to the position expressed by the deputy mayor, Palazzo Civico will remain a landmark and an institutional seat of the City. For example, sessions of the legislature will continue to be held in the building. The motion therefore forms part of the discussion on how to pair this institutional function with a public and cultural use of any spaces that may become available.
However, the administrative step is not presented as already completed. The proposal speaks of a future relocation and spaces that would be vacated; the museum is presented as an option to be considered. The discussion is thus linked to two elements: the relocation to Cornaredo and the determination of the use of the second floor. ... ## The follow-up and issues still open
For the time being, the motion opens an assessment but does not establish the launch of a museum. Roberto Badaracco said he was willing to examine the proposal further. He did, however, recall that the transfer of some of the staff currently working at Palazzo Civico has not yet been decided. This leaves it to be determined which rooms will actually be available and when, without turning the plan indicated in the motion into an already operational certainty.
The timing of the Pse also remains to be verified. The parliamentary motion links the relocation of the second-floor offices to 2028, but the deputy mayor pointed out that it is not certain that the Pse towers will already have been built in two years. The possibility of freeing up the spaces therefore depends on a transfer to Cornaredo and on the availability of the East Tower, elements that the source presents as still requiring verification.
### Archives, storage facilities and management
If the planned relocation were to take place, according to the motion the second floor would make it possible to exhibit other objects currently kept in archives and storage facilities that are not easily accessible to the public. This reference broadens the proposal beyond the works and objects already visible in the corridors. The proposed historical museum would therefore also potentially contain materials that are not currently on display, if the vacated spaces were assigned this function.
However, the question of management remains open. Badaracco warned: «A permanent museum would entail the presence of a permanent curator». The presence of a curator is one of the points to be considered in the assessment.
The follow-up indicated by the motion is therefore a debate on the future of Palazzo Civico and a closer examination of the proposal. No definitive decision on the exhibition setup is reported: on the one hand, the transfer of the staff is still uncertain; on the other, the timing of the Pse towers remains to be verified. The discussion will have to bring together the question of the building’s cultural purpose and the functions already present in the building. The next step documented by the source therefore remains an assessment, while the spaces, timing and arrangements for any potential museum are still under discussion.

item.description: Finance Director Christian Vitta presents the 2027 budget: possible debt exceeding 3 billion and a 360-degree review of revenue.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 2027 deficit close to 100 million francs - Possible debt exceeding 3 billion at the end of 2027 - Vitta presents his final budget - A package for the next four years is being considered
- What → the Canton’s budget for 2027 - Deficit → close to 100 million francs - Impact of the measures → approximately 237 million francs - Interviewee → Christian Vitta, director of the Department of Finance and Economics - Possible debt → over 3 billion at the end of 2027
The 2027 budget of the Canton of Ticino closes with an operating deficit close to 100 million francs. The budget shows a shortfall approaching that threshold, but political discussion focuses mainly on what will come next: the near future and the construction of a vision for the cantonal accounts.
To present the figures, Christian Vitta, State Councillor and director of the Department of Finance and Economics, was interviewed by RSI’s SEIDISERA radio programme. This is his final budget: Vitta will not stand for re-election next April.
### The framework left by the legislature
According to Vitta, during the legislature, interventions on individual budgets produced an overall impact of approximately 237 million francs. In his account, the figure is equivalent to a multi-year package spread over several years. The choice was linked to a situation described as rapidly evolving.
Meanwhile, the framework has been enriched by three fixed points identified by the director himself: the impact of initiatives concerning health insurance funds, the federal decision on EFAS and imputed rental value. Vitta stressed that these elements were not yet present at the beginning of the legislature.
This has led to the possibility of addressing a multi-year package as well, as already happened in 2016. However, the precedent is not presented as a guarantee. Vitta referred to the case of the Canton of Fribourg, where a proposal pursued along those lines was rejected by 70% of the population. In his view, the risk is having to start from scratch. Despite this, the data point towards a package covering the next four years.
The same logic applies to sectoral reforms. In principle, Vitta explained, agreement can be broad; when it comes to individual sectors, divergences, friction and divisions emerge. The example cited is the debate over a unified police force.
Regarding revenue, the director ruled out a discussion limited solely to taxation. The reasoning will have to encompass various areas and seek any room for manoeuvre. A general increase, he observed, is difficult for the population to accept, while in other Cantons the opposite course has also been seen, with taxes being reduced.
> «So the discussion will have to be conducted from every angle.»
The budget thus opens a discussion concerning the immediate deficit, possible debt exceeding three billion at the end of 2027 and the decisions that will have to follow. It contains no specific measure for cross-border workers. For those who work between Italy and the Canton of Ticino, the text does not indicate tax rates, personal amounts or an already approved change to be translated into an individual calculation. The calcolatore fiscale may be used when any concrete measures are defined. For those who work across the border, the practical significance of the news lies in distinguishing a cantonal forecast from a decision applicable to everyday life. The text discusses revenue, taxes, expenditure and debt; however, it does not indicate a measure intended for cross-border workers, nor an individual amount to be applied.
The source neither mentions nor quantifies any measure concerning a G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates or withholding tax. For a cross-border worker, this delimitation is precise: the budget concerns the Canton of Ticino, but it does not allow one to say that withholdings, social security, insurance or tax relations with Italy will change.
### The actual scope of the news
| Topic | Source's indication | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Revenue | The discussion must cover several items, not just taxes. | No across-the-board increase is indicated. | | Expenditure | Guerra calls for cuts; Durisch argues that cuts alone are not enough. | No reduction has yet been defined. | | Package | The focus is on an intervention over the next four years. | The text does not mention an approved package. | | Debt | It could exceed three billion at the end of 2027. | This is a cantonal outlook, not an individual amount. | | 2027 result | Agustoni envisages a balanced result or figures close to balance. | The outcome remains tied to the estimates and the 2026 final accounts. |
The group leaders are divided over how to interpret the deficit. Maurizio Agustoni urges people not to be impressed by the figure of -98 million: he considers the Swiss National Bank's dividends conservative and believes it is possible to close with a balanced result or close to balance, also looking at the 2026 final accounts. This is an assessment of the expected result, not an announcement of a tax change.
The other positions concern how to intervene. Government President Marina Carobbio Guscetti does not consider a tax increase taboo. Ivo Durisch considers it worth evaluating because, in his view, resolving the situation solely through cuts is impossible. Alain Bühler considers taxes the ultima ratio and calls first for corrective measures. Michele Guerra announces a minority report and proposes acting on expenditure. Matteo Quadranti calls the budget pre-election and calls for a change of pace.
For a cross-border worker, these are political positions to follow, not rules already in force. Until the measure chosen is specified, even strumento per la dichiarazione dei redditi cannot derive a new rate or a new personal amount from the budget alone.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. The text does not assign the cross-border worker a form, a deadline or a new withholding. The procedure that can be built on the basis of the source is therefore a four-step monitoring process, not an obligation that is already in force.
### Four steps for following developments
1. Separate the figure from the proposal. The starting point is the projected deficit for 2027, close to 100 million francs. It must be kept separate from the subsequent political assumptions: the text does not yet present an individual tax measure.
2. Distinguish revenue from expenditure. Every future proposal should be assessed by checking whether it concerns taxation, other areas of revenue or spending cuts. Vitta calls for a 360-degree review; Durisch, Bühler and Guerra, by contrast, point to different priorities for putting the accounts back in order.
3. Record the political deadlines already indicated. Vitta will not stand for re-election next April. The possible package has a four-year time horizon, while debt is projected through the end of 2027. These are the time references given in the text; no other operational deadlines for cross-border workers are indicated.
4. Wait for data that may change the interpretation. Agustoni refers to the 2026 final accounts and the National Bank’s cautious estimate of dividends. Before translating the projected deficit into a personal impact, it is therefore necessary to wait until the applicable measures and figures have been specified.
The source does not indicate any offices, documents to be submitted or tax procedures linked to the budget. Therefore, the concrete step today is not to attribute to the -98 million an effect that the text does not quantify. When amounts or actual measures become available, simulatore busta paga will allow you to compare a personal scenario. To verify the tax impact of the final decision, use calcolatore fiscale.

item.title: Accident on the SS707 in Varese, link road closed for hours
item.description: Collision between two cars on SS707 at the outskirts of Varese: the link road between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange closed for hours. Two injured, yellow code.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Collision between two cars on the SS707 on the outskirts of Varese - SS707 closed for hours between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange - Traffic diverted toward the city center - Two people assisted: a man aged 55 and a woman aged 67
## Key facts - What → collision between two vehicles - Road → SS707, connection to the A8 motorway - Alert → 7.02 - Closure → for hours, in both directions - Diversion → toward the city center - People assisted → 55-year-old man and 67-year-old woman - Outcome → yellow code
### The accident on the SS707 At 7.02 the alert was raised on the outskirts of Varese for an accident along the SS707, the state road connecting to the A8 motorway. The accident involved two cars and made it necessary to close the affected section to allow rescue operations, investigations, and traffic management.
The SS707 remained closed for several hours between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange, with traffic halted in both directions. Law enforcement closed the section at Largo Flaiano for vehicles heading toward Milan, while the operation at the scene was still underway.
The first information came from the AREU operations center, Soreu Laghi. The accident involved two people who were assisted: a 55-year-old man and a 67-year-old woman. This was the initial account reported for the accident between the two cars.
The Traffic Police also diverted the flow of cars toward the city center, near the Laghi interchange. The measure was adopted together with the closure, so as to allow the planned activities on the state-road section. The effect on traffic was immediate: slowdowns and queues in the area providing access to the provincial capital.
The initial medical assessment indicated a yellow code for the people involved. The source reports that they sustained serious injuries, but not injuries considered severe enough to put their lives at risk. The two road references contained in the report are therefore Largo Flaiano, the closure point for vehicles heading toward Milan, and the Laghi interchange, from which traffic was diverted toward the city center. ## Traffic management
### The closed section and the diverted flow The morning's traffic management concerned the road connection with the A8 motorway. The source identifies SS707 as the state road affected by the accident and places the closure between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange. The measure, which lasted several hours, affected both directions of travel; near Largo Flaiano, the section was closed to vehicles heading toward Milan.
At the interchange for the Laghi, however, the flow of cars was directed toward the city center. The State Police managed this diversion while rescue operations, accident investigations and traffic management continued. The route taken by cars was thus shifted to the access area to the provincial capital, where the source reports slowdowns and queues.
The description of the traffic situation identifies two distinct points of the operation: Largo Flaiano, where the closure for vehicles heading toward Milan was concentrated, and the Laghi interchange, used to divert traffic toward the center. The SS707 section remained at the center of the activities required after the collision.
### Operations at the scene Alongside the State Police, the Varese Fire Brigade and the Varese Local Police intervened at the scene. The Fire Brigade worked to secure the area, while the Local Police took part in managing traffic. Rescue vehicles from the Varese Red Cross also arrived.
The activities indicated in the source therefore addressed three immediate needs: securing the area, assisting the people involved and regulating traffic. The closure of the state road made it possible to carry out these operations together with the accident investigations, while the diversion directed cars toward the city center. The result described for access to Varese was a morning marked by queues and slowdowns, while the responding forces managed traffic. ## Traffic reopened
### The medical toll After hours of closure and on-site operations, the source update reports that traffic has reopened. The SS707 was therefore reopened after the difficult morning described on the outskirts of Varese, at the end of the phase during which the section between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange had remained closed for hours.
For the people involved, the rescue process continued after the initial treatment provided on site. The source reports that they were transported to hospital and specifies that one of the injured people was taken into care and evacuated to the Ospedale di Circolo di Varese.
The yellow code declared for the people involved describes serious injuries, but without danger to life. In the report, this is the medical toll associated with the collision between the two cars: two people assisted, initial treatment on site and subsequent transfer to hospital.
### The latest update The documented follow-up concerns traffic: traffic was reopened after the closure that lasted for hours and after the flow was diverted toward the city center. The previous phase had involved the section between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange and had caused slowdowns and queues in the access area to the provincial capital.
The operational sequence indicated by the source includes rescue operations, investigations and traffic management. First, the people received treatment on site; then transport to hospital was arranged. On the road, the closure affected the indicated segment, while the diversion had been organized at the Laghi interchange.
The final update to the news therefore combines reopened traffic and assistance to the two people involved, with one of the injured people directed to the Ospedale di Circolo di Varese. For the morning of the accident on the outskirts of Varese, these are the developments reported by the source.

## In brief - Serious accident in the afternoon on the A2 in Coldrerio - Car crashes into truck in the emergency lay-by - The 73-year-old passenger is in life-threatening condition - The 68-year-old driver sustained minor injuries

In the afternoon, on highway 2 southbound in the Coldrerio area, a car rear-ended a truck stopped at the side of the roadway, in the emergency lay-by. For reasons yet to be established, the circumstances of the rear-end collision have not been clarified. The initial information was collected by Rescue Media and then confirmed by the Cantonal Police.
The car was being driven by a 68-year-old Swiss woman residing in the canton of Zurich, who sustained minor injuries. A 73-year-old Swiss man, also residing in the canton of Zurich, was in the vehicle as a passenger. The man's injuries were serious and life-threatening.
The initial account reported by the source therefore speaks of two injured people, with different outcomes for the driver and the passenger. The time reference indicated in the report is the afternoon, while the article update is marked at 17:45.
The accident occurred along the southbound carriageway of the A2, in the Coldrerio area. The truck was stopped at the side of the roadway, in the emergency lay-by; the car rear-ended it for reasons that remain to be established. Officers from the Polizia cantonale arrived at the scene. The Pompieri del Mendrisiotto arrived to provide support. The operation also involved rescuers from the Servizio Autoambulanza Mendrisiotto, referred to in the source by the acronym SAM, and Rega.

item.title: Swiss inflation: +1% in September driven by fuel
item.description: Swiss inflation rises by 1% annually in September: fuels lead the way, with heating oil +65%, diesel +28,7% and petrol +19,9%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Annual inflation at 1% in September - In August it was already at 0,8% - Heating oil +65%, diesel +28,7% - Gasoline +19,9%; monthly CPI stable
## Key facts - Institutional source → FSO - Annual inflation in September → 1% - Annual inflation in August → 0,8% - Monthly CPI → stable - AWP forecasts → between 0,7% and 1,2% annually; between -0,3% and +0,2% monthly
### The change measured in September
Inflation in Switzerland accelerated by 1% year on year in September. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO) reported this on Thursday, explaining that consumer prices, already up 0,8% in August, continued to rise in the month just ended.
According to the statement, the biggest boost came from the surge in fuel prices. The text links this movement to the war in the Middle East. This is the figure that sets the tone for the September reading: the general increase in prices is presented alongside the sharp rise in fuel-related items.
### Year and month tell two different stories
By contrast, the comparison with the previous month shows a flat picture. The consumer price index (CPI) remained stable because, according to federal statisticians, opposing trends largely offset each other. The monthly figure therefore does not erase the increase observed year on year, but shows that the index's overall balance did not change between August and September.
The development was in line with the forecasts of economists surveyed by the AWP agency. For September, annual inflation was expected to be between 0,7% and 1,2%; the monthly change was forecast to be between -0,3% and +0,2%. The expectations therefore concerned two different measures, which should not be conflated with the annual figure of 1%.
### Fuel contributions
Year on year, the largest contributors to the rise in prices were heating oil, at +65%, diesel, at +28,7%, and gasoline, at +19,9%. The statement lists these three items among the drivers of the month, without providing any additional prices per litre or a breakdown by consumer categories.
The source finally broaches the subject of oil prices, indicating that further increases are on the horizon, but the text does not add a figure or date to quantify them. This distinction is also essential: the observed result is 1% year on year in September, while the outlook for possible future increases remains unquantified in the statement. ### What it means for the cross-border commuter
For a cross-border commuter who uses a car, the most direct practical connection is the fuel item. item.title: Noranco car theft: three arrests and vehicles recovered
item.description: Three high-end cars stolen in Noranco have been recovered. Three people, a 20-year-old Italian national, a 21-year-old Algerian national and a 25-year-old French national, residing in France, were detained.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Three high-end cars stolen in Noranco - Theft reported shortly after 2.30 - Three people detained in Manno, Tenero and Lucerne - Vehicles recovered in Breganzona, Manno and Gordola
## Key facts - Location → Pambio-Noranco - Vehicles → three high-end cars - Detained → 20-year-old Italian national, 21-year-old Algerian national, 25-year-old French national - Residence → all in France - Coordination → public prosecutor Luca Losa - Checks → fedpol-cantonal police task force
PAMBIO-NORANCO - Three high-end cars were stolen overnight from a garage in Noranco and subsequently recovered. Three people were arrested in different locations. The operation was announced by the Public Prosecutor's Office and the Cantonal Police.
The burglary was reported shortly after 2.30 last night. According to initial findings, the perpetrators first stole the keys to three vehicles, then took the cars and fled.
Searches and investigations initiated immediately made it possible to locate the stolen vehicles and detain three people: in Manno, a 20-year-old Italian national; in Tenero, a 21-year-old Algerian national; and in Lucerne, a 25-year-old French national. All three reside in France. The vehicles were recovered in Breganzona, Manno and Gordola.
The alleged offences include theft, violation of domicile, criminal damage, infringement of the Federal Road Traffic Act and infringement of the Federal Act on Foreign Nationals and Integration.
### The operation's network In addition to the Ticino Cantonal Police, the cantonal police forces of Graubünden, Uri, Valais and Lucerne took part in the operation. Several Ticino municipal police forces, the Transport Police and the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security also took part.
The joint investigative task force of the Federal Office of Police, fedpol, and the cantonal police forces is checking for possible links to similar cases and the possible involvement of other people. The investigation is coordinated by public prosecutor Luca Losa. Given that investigations are still under way, no further information will be provided for the time being. ## The sequence that emerges
### From the theft of the keys to the recovery The reconstruction communicated by the authorities follows a precise order: first the break-in at the garage, then the theft of the keys, followed by the theft of the three cars and the getaway. The information therefore distinguishes access to the garage from the subsequent departure of the vehicles.
The geographical distribution is also defined in two different stages. The three people were arrested in Manno, Tenero and Lucerne, while the cars were recovered in Breganzona, Manno and Gordola. The source lists these places separately and provides no further details on the correspondence between individual arrests and individual vehicles.
For those who live or work in Canton Ticino, including a cross-border commuter who travels by car, the practical relevance remains limited to the security of garages, keys and vehicles. No issue related to cross-border work, home-to-work routes or other administrative aspects is described: the news concerns an investigation into burglary.
The second element to consider is the scope of the investigation. It does not involve only the Ticino Cantonal Police: the statement lists cantonal forces from several regions, Ticino municipal police forces, the Transport Police, fedpol and UDSC. The presence of a joint task force now serves to verify any links with similar cases and the possible involvement of other people.
The offenses under consideration include vehicle theft, access to the garage, damage, road traffic and legislation concerning foreign nationals and their integration. However, the statement does not anticipate the outcome of the inquiries and specifies that no further information will be released while the investigation is still ongoing.
Movements and travel times are not addressed in the source. For these separate topics, tempi attesa valichi and mezzi pubblici Ticino can be consulted.

### Protecting spaces Authorities first of all remind people to protect spaces with adequate lighting, barriers and anti-theft systems for doors and windows. This guidance directly concerns the garage, that is, the place from which the keys and subsequently the vehicles were taken.
The second step concerns the safekeeping of keys and valuables. Keys, cash and valuable items should be kept in safe places, including the safes indicated by the authorities. For vehicles, the reminder is to use the available security systems.
### Monitoring and activating the alarm The third measure consists of installing electronic systems capable of promptly detecting intrusions and activating the alarm. The three recommendations can be applied in sequence: first protect doors and windows, then secure keys and valuables, and finally add a detection system.
For a cross-border commuter who leaves a car in a garage, this is the practically useful part of the news. It does not require reconstructing the dynamics of the arrests or anticipating the task force's work: it focuses attention on access points, keys, anti-theft systems and surveillance.
